title: INT8/FP16 curriculum calibration and cosine-probe for embedding stability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Build and validate a repeatable 'curriculum' calibration workflow for INT8 and FP16 embedding profiles and add a lightweight cosine-probe that detects early drift during canary rollouts. The curriculum approach stages calibration datasets from 'core anchors' -> 'expanded corpora' -> 'edge cases', so we can quantify accuracy loss as embeddings move from FP32 -> FP16 -> INT8. Deliverables: 1) calibration harness and sampling policy, 2) automated cosine-probe dashboard and alerting, 3) canary rollout gating rules and remediation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can run full curriculum on 10k anchor vectors in under 2 hours for a single model variant
Cosine-probe dashboard shows per-corpus median and 95th percentile drift and alerts when median drop exceeds 0.015 relative to baseline
Canary policy blocks INT8 rollout if any critical corpus shows median cosine fall > 0.02 or ARI (anchor regression index) > 0.01
End-to-end test (PR) includes synthetic regression case and automatic rollback simulation in staging
steps: Design curriculum: identify 3 tiers of corpora (anchors, mid-size reference, long-tail) with target sample sizes
Implement sampling tool: deterministic seeded sampling so runs are reproducible across calibrations
Extend calibration pipeline to emit per-layer quantization stats and reconstructed FP32->quantized embedding pairs
Compute similarity matrix per-corpus and summarize median, mean, 5th, 95th percentiles; persist in metrics store
Build cosine-probe service that compares current run to baseline snapshot and produces drift indicators
Wire alerts in Grafana: sustain windows of 1h and 24h with cooldowns to avoid noisy flips
Create canary gating rules in rollout controller: allow/deny rules + auto-fallback to FP16 if thresholds triggered
Document playbook for ops: triage steps, re-calibration, temporary model pinning, and postmortem template

decisions: Use curriculum staging instead of single mixed dataset to better isolate which corpus tiers are sensitive to quantization
Baseline snapshot will be the latest FP32 production run taken immediately before any INT8 experiment; store with commit hash and run_id
Alerting thresholds set conservatively to reduce false positives: median_drop=0.015 (warning), median_drop=0.02 (critical)
If a critical corpus crosses threshold during canary, automatically fallback to FP16 variant and create an incident for on-call to investigate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long-tail corpora amplify variance and can cause noisy alerts. Mitigation: use stratified sampling and smoothing windows; require sustained window before action
Risk: Calibration compute cost could be high at scale. Mitigation: incremental curriculum runs (anchors nightly, full curriculum weekly) and cached quantization artifacts
Risk: Canary false negative where drift appears only at higher query rates. Mitigation: include QPS-scaled stress runs during pre-rollout testing
